paper_metadata.title: LFM2 Technical Report
paper_metadata.abstract: We present LFM2, a family of Liquid Foundation Models designed for efficient on-device deployment and strong task capabilities. Using hardware-in-the-loop architecture search under edge latency and memory constraints, we obtain a compact hybrid backbone that combines gated short convolutions with a small number of grouped query attention blocks, delivering up to 2x faster prefill and decode on CPUs compared to similarly sized models. The LFM2 family covers 350M-8.3B parameters, including dense models (350M, 700M, 1.2B, 2.6B) and a mixture-of-experts variant (8.3B total, 1.5B active), all with 32K context length. LFM2's training pipeline includes a tempered, decoupled Top-K knowledge distillation objective that avoids support mismatch; curriculum learning with difficulty-ordered data; and a three-stage post-training recipe of supervised fine-tuning, length-normalized preference optimization, and model merging. Pre-trained on 10-12T tokens, LFM2 models achieve strong results across diverse benchmarks; for example, LFM2-2.6B reaches 79.56% on IFEval and 82.41% on GSM8K. We further build multimodal and retrieval variants: LFM2-VL for vision-language tasks, LFM2-Audio for speech, and LFM2-ColBERT for retrieval. LFM2-VL supports tunable accuracy-latency tradeoffs via token-efficient visual processing, while LFM2-Audio separates audio input and output pathways to enable real-time speech-to-speech interaction competitive with models 3x larger. LFM2-ColBERT provides a low-latency encoder for queries and documents, enabling high-performance retrieval across multiple languages. All models are released with open weights and deployment packages for ExecuTorch, llama.cpp, and vLLM, making LFM2 a practical base for edge applications that need fast, memory-efficient inference and strong task capabilities.

extraction_data.innovation: Hardware-in-the-loop architecture search: Pareto optimization over quality, latency, and peak memory to select a minimal hybrid backbone; Gated short convolutions for most layers combined with a small minority of grouped-query attention (GQA) layers to recover quality deficits without additional SSMs or linear-attention operators; designed to maximize downstream quality while staying within tight device-side budgets on CPUs and heterogeneous NPUs.
extraction_data.pretraining_corpus: ~75% English text, ~20% multilingual text (Japanese, Arabic, Korean, Spanish, French, German), ~5% code
extraction_data.finetuning_task: Supervised instruction tuning, preference alignment, Supervised fine-tuning
extraction_data.hardware_used: Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3), AMD Ryzen HX 370
extraction_data.extension: Augments the language backbone with a SigLIP2 vision encoder and a lightweight connector to enable flexible accuracy-latency trade-offs on device.
extraction_data.research_problem: Small models for edge devices supporting 32K contexts, multimodal inputs, and retrieval
extraction_data.application: Short-to-medium context interactions, task-oriented applications, edge deployments with tight latency and memory budgets
extraction_data.finetuning_data: Open-source and proprietary instruction and preference data (~1M conversations), ~5.39M samples (dense), 9.24M samples (8B-A1B); 67/79 curated sources, Mixture of transcription, classification, TTS, and audio-chat data
extraction_data.supported_language: English, Japanese, Arabic, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Multilingual, European languages
extraction_data.attention_mechanism: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) with QK-Norm; interleaved with gated short convolution blocks, Gated short convolutions + Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
extraction_data.training_pipeline: Three-stage post-training pipeline including long-context mid-training and decoupled Top-K distillation objective
extraction_data.synthetic_data_generation_method: In-house synthetic datasets generated for specialized audio chat capabilities
extraction_data.fusion_architecture: MLP connector aligning audio encoder to LFM2 backbone

extraction_data.innovation: Decoupled, tempered Top-K knowledge distillation objective that avoids support mismatch by decomposing KL divergence into a binary mass-matching term and a conditional KL within the Top-K set; edge-first architecture optimized for CPU inference throughput and latency.

extraction_data.innovation: Liquid Foundation Model (LFM2) architecture: uses liquid neural networks/state-space models for efficient next-token prediction, enabling strong multimodal performance at small scales (<4B parameters) with significantly less training and inference-time compute compared to prior VLMs; Adaptable performance vs. latency scaling: varies the maximum number of vision tokens per image at inference by adjusting the preprocessing pipeline, allowing graceful performance degradation and on-device latency tuning without retraining; Multilingual visual understanding: surpasses Qwen2.5-VL-3B on translated MMBench and MMMB, outperforming all other open-source models under 4B parameters; Language-only tasks: maintains strong language capabilities (MMLU 62.70, MMMLU 53.37) despite multimodal optimization, closely matching larger baselines.

extraction_data.innovation: Late interaction (ColBERT-style) architecture with a hybrid LFM2 backbone (10 convolutional + 6 attention blocks) and a linear projection head for fine-grained token-level similarity matching, trained via knowledge distillation from a powerful cross-encoder teacher using the PyLate framework.
extraction_data.application: Information retrieval, fact verification, question answering, entity retrieval

extraction_data.training_pipeline: Continued pre-training of LFM2-350M to 25T tokens, followed by knowledge distillation training with 9 task-specific layers added to the backbone.
